raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both studies are readable full texts produced under the same two research programmes—UNHIDE and Horizon 2020 Marie Sklodowska-Curie INHAbIT Cities (Grant No. 656738)—by overlapping author teams (Cecilia Alda-Vidal and Maria Rusca) studying the same municipal utility, the Lilongwe Water Board (LWB) in Lilongwe, Malawi (and citing the same city-level baseline figures: 78% network coverage split between 44% in-house connections and 56% water kiosks). However, their empirical fieldwork datasets, respondent samples, legal/operational exposures, and outcomes are distinct. Study A (Pihljak et al., 2019/2021) examines the multi-level governance and negotiation of water tariffs across three fieldwork waves (2008-2009 on WUA establishment; Nov 2013-Jan 2014 comparative tariff interviews corresponding to Pihljak's 2014 MSc thesis; and Oct 2017-June 2018 follow-up interviews and 2018 documentary screenings conducted after Study B's February 2017 online publication), interviewing GoM officials, LWB/Kiosk Management Unit staff, seven WUAs, NGOs, and residents of two LIAs alongside 2006-2018 tariff and WUA financial records. Study B (Alda-Vidal et al., 2017/2018) is an ethnographic and participatory mapping study conducted over four months in 2014 comprising 38 semi-structured interviews with LWB technical operators, engineers, and managers, a focus group discussion, and participant observation of physical operation and maintenance (backup line diversions, pressurized take-offs, unrecorded valve operations, and repair prioritization) shaping spatial inequalities in supply continuity and pressure. Study A also cites Study B (Alda-Vidal et al., 2018) and Pihljak's 2014 thesis is cited separately in Study B. Double-counting risk is low because the designs, respondent groups, and outcomes (water pricing vs physical O&M continuity) are distinct, though systematic reviewers aggregating at the city or utility level should note both examine the same single utility (LWB).
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Lilongwe, Malawi (Lilongwe Water Board [LWB] in-house connection regime and LWB-Water Users Association [WUA] kiosk regime). Qualitative multi-phase fieldwork conducted in 2008-2009, 2013-2014 (Nov 2013-Jan 2014), and 2017-2018 (Oct 2017-June 2018), comprising semi-structured interviews with representatives of the Government of Malawi (GoM), LWB (including Kiosk Management Unit), seven WUAs, local NGOs, and residents of two low-income areas (LIAs), supplemented by 2018 documentary screenings and 2006-2018 tariff, revenue, and WUA financial surplus records (exact total interview N not reported).
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: Lilongwe, Malawi (Lilongwe Water Board [LWB] centralized piped water network across northern, central, and southern zones). Qualitative fieldwork conducted over four months in 2014 comprising N = 38 semi-structured interviews with LWB employees from operators and engineers to managers (plus a Ministry representative and international expert), participatory hotspot mapping of service continuity, a focus group discussion, and participant observation following LWB technical staff in daily operation and maintenance activities.
